title: WhatsApp for Communication & Business
subtitle: Set up WhatsApp safely, communicate clearly with family, groups and communities, and run a small business with WhatsApp Business tools.
description: A practical course on the real features of WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business, from installing and securing your account to groups, channels, communities, catalogues, quick replies and labels. Every lesson ends with a task on your own phone, and the course closes with a complete, scam-aware WhatsApp setup for your work or community.
outcomes: Install, back up and secure WhatsApp with privacy settings and two-step verification
Write clear messages and choose the right tool: text, voice note, call, document or status
Run groups, broadcast lists, channels and communities without exposing members or causing noise
Set up a complete WhatsApp Business profile with catalogue, greeting and away messages, quick replies and labels
Recognise common WhatsApp scams and respond safely to protect yourself and your customers
audience: Women who use a smartphone and want to communicate confidently, run community groups or sell products and services on WhatsApp.
tools: An Android phone or iPhone with a data bundle or Wi-Fi
The WhatsApp Business app (free), ideally with a second SIM
A Google or iCloud account for backups
Paper and pen for plans and PINs

modules.title: Getting Started Safely with WhatsApp
modules.overview: You will install WhatsApp correctly, protect your account with privacy settings and two-step verification, organise your contacts, and learn your way around every tab and icon. By the end of this module your account is set up the way a careful professional sets hers up.

lessons.title: Installing WhatsApp and verifying your number
objectives: Download the genuine WhatsApp or WhatsApp Business app from the official store
Verify your phone number with the six-digit code and set your profile name
Choose between the personal app and the Business app for your situation
Back up your chats so you do not lose them when you change phones

blocks.text: WhatsApp is a free app for sending messages, voice notes, photos, documents and for making voice and video calls over the internet. It uses your **data bundle or Wi-Fi**, not your call credit, so a call to your sister in London costs you only the data it uses. Your account is tied to **one phone number**. The number becomes your WhatsApp identity, so choose a line you plan to keep for years.

blocks.name: mobile-app
blocks.alt: A woman holding a large smartphone showing an app screen
blocks.caption: Everything in this course starts with the right app installed on your phone.

blocks.text: Two apps, one family

There are two official apps, both free. **WhatsApp Messenger** (usually just called WhatsApp) is for personal use. **WhatsApp Business** is a separate app made for small businesses. It adds a business profile, a catalogue, automatic greeting and away messages, quick replies and labels. You can run both on the same phone if you use **two different numbers**, for example your personal MTN line in one and your business Airtel line in the other.

blocks.title: Which app should you install?
items: WhatsApp (personal)
WhatsApp Business
blocks.caption: Install the personal app for your private life and the Business app when you sell or offer a service.

blocks.text: Getting the genuine app

Only install WhatsApp from the **Google Play Store** on Android phones or the **App Store** on iPhones. Search for WhatsApp, and check that the developer is listed as **WhatsApp LLC**. Never install versions passed around as files on WhatsApp or Telegram, such as "GB WhatsApp" or other modified copies. They are not made by WhatsApp, they can steal your messages, and WhatsApp can ban accounts that use them.

blocks.title: Modified WhatsApp apps are a trap
blocks.text: Apps that promise extra features like hiding blue ticks or seeing deleted messages are unofficial. They put your chats, photos and bank details at risk. If you have one, back up what you need, uninstall it and install the official app.
Verifying your number

items: Open the app and agree to the terms of service.
Select Nigeria (+234) as your country and type your number without the first zero, for example 803 123 4567.
Wait for an SMS with a **six-digit verification code**. Many Android phones read it automatically. If the SMS does not come, choose the option to get the code by phone call.
Type in your **profile name**. This is the name people see when you message them if they have not saved your number. Use your real name or business name, not a nickname like "Sweet Mummy".
Add a clear **profile photo**, then allow WhatsApp to find your contacts if you want your saved contacts to appear.

blocks.title: Your code is like your ATM PIN
blocks.text: The six-digit code proves the number is yours. WhatsApp will never call or message you to ask for it. Anyone who gets your code can take over your account and message your contacts asking for money. Never share it, even with a friend who says the code was sent to you by mistake.
Backing up so you never lose your chats

Your messages live on your phone, not on WhatsApp's servers. If the phone is stolen or spoilt and you have no backup, the chats are gone. On Android, go to **Settings, Chats, Chat backup** and link your **Google account** (Google Drive). On iPhone, the backup goes to **iCloud**. Set the backup frequency to daily or weekly, and choose whether to include videos, because videos make the backup large and use more data. Many people choose to back up only on Wi-Fi to save their bundle.

blocks.title: Worked example: moving WhatsApp to a new phone
blocks.context: For example, Bisi in Ibadan buys a new Android phone and wants her customers' chats on it. Her old phone still works.
steps: On the old phone she opens Settings, Chats, Chat backup and taps Back up, while connected to Wi-Fi.
She checks the screen shows the backup time as just now, linked to her Google account.
She inserts her SIM in the new phone, installs WhatsApp from the Play Store and signs in to the same Google account.
She verifies her number with the six-digit SMS code.
WhatsApp finds the backup and offers to Restore. She taps Restore and waits while the chats load, then the media.
blocks.result: All her chats and voice notes appear on the new phone. She now leaves daily backup switched on.

blocks.text: If your old phone is lost, you can still restore from Google Drive or iCloud on the new phone, as long as you had backups switched on before the loss. First get a replacement SIM with the same number from your network's office, then install WhatsApp and verify. Verifying on a new phone also logs the old phone out of WhatsApp, which protects you if a thief has it.
Keep the app updated

WhatsApp regularly fixes security problems and adds features. Open the Play Store or App Store every few weeks, search WhatsApp and tap **Update** if you see it, or switch on automatic updates. Some of the features in this course will only appear if your app is up to date, and menu names can shift a little between updates and between Android and iPhone.

takeaways: Install only from Play Store or App Store, developer WhatsApp LLC.
Your account is tied to one number; the six-digit code is never shared.
Use the personal app for private life and WhatsApp Business for selling.
Switch on chat backup to Google Drive or iCloud before you need it.

activity.title: Set up and back up
steps: Check that your WhatsApp app comes from the official store and is up to date.
Set your profile name to your real name or business name.
Open Settings, Chats, Chat backup and switch on backup to Google Drive or iCloud.
Run one backup now on Wi-Fi and note the date and time shown.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of your Chat backup screen showing the last backup time.

lessons.title: Your profile, privacy settings and two-step verification
objectives: Set who can see your last seen, profile photo, about and status
Control who can add you to groups and silence unknown callers
Switch on two-step verification with a six-digit PIN and email
Use the Privacy checkup to review your settings in one place

blocks.text: Your WhatsApp profile tells people who you are. Your privacy settings decide **how much of it strangers can see**. A good setup lets customers and colleagues recognise you while keeping your personal life and your account safe. All the settings in this lesson are in **Settings, Privacy** and **Settings, Account**.

blocks.name: mobile-encryption
blocks.alt: A phone with a padlock on the screen
blocks.caption: Privacy settings and two-step verification are the locks on your WhatsApp account.

blocks.text: Your profile

items: **Profile photo:** a clear, friendly picture of your face, or your logo for a business. Avoid photos of your children here.
**Name:** the name shown to people who have not saved your number.
**About:** a short line such as "Fashion designer, Abeokuta" or "Available 8am to 6pm".
**Phone number:** shown to anyone you chat with. You cannot hide it in normal chats.

blocks.text: Who can see what

For each item in Settings, Privacy you choose from options such as **Everyone**, **My contacts**, **My contacts except...** and **Nobody**. "My contacts" means people saved in your phone's contact list. The table shows a sensible setup for most women using WhatsApp for both family and small business.

head: Setting
What it controls
Suggested choice
rows: Whether people see when you were last on WhatsApp
Who can read your short description
Everyone (if it is about your work) or My contacts
My contacts, or My contacts except...
Blue ticks that show you read a message
Your choice; if off, you also cannot see others' blue ticks
Who can add you to groups
My contacts except..., or My contacts
Calls from numbers you have not saved go quiet
On, if you get spam calls

blocks.text: Changing **Groups** to My contacts stops strangers from adding you to investment, crypto or "forex trading" groups, which is one of the most common ways scams begin. **Silence unknown callers** sends calls from unsaved numbers straight to your call list without ringing, so you can decide later whether to call back.

blocks.title: Use Privacy checkup
blocks.text: Under Settings, Privacy you will find Privacy checkup. It walks you through who can contact you, what personal information is visible, and how to add more protection to your account, all on a few simple screens.
Two-step verification: the most important setting

Two-step verification adds a **six-digit PIN that you create**. After it is on, anyone trying to register your number on a new phone needs both the SMS code and your PIN. Even if a fraudster tricks you or your network into giving away the SMS code, they still cannot get in without the PIN.

blocks.title: How two-step verification blocks a hijacker
items: Fraudster gets SMS code
WhatsApp asks for PIN
Fraudster does not know it
Account stays yours
blocks.caption: The PIN is a second lock that the SMS code alone cannot open.

items: Open Settings, then Account, then Two-step verification.
Tap Turn on (or Create PIN) and type a six-digit PIN you will remember. Do not use your birthday, 123456 or your ATM PIN.
Type it again to confirm.
Add an **email address** you can open. WhatsApp uses it to send you a reset link if you forget the PIN. You can skip it, but it is wiser to add it.
Write the PIN somewhere safe at home, not in your phone notes.

blocks.text: WhatsApp will sometimes ask you to enter the PIN while you use the app. This is normal: it helps you remember it. Never type your PIN into a link someone sends you, and never read it to anyone on the phone.

blocks.title: Worked example: a near miss
blocks.context: For example, Chioma in Owerri sells hair products. One evening she gets a message from her cousin's account: "I mistakenly sent my code to your number, please send it to me." At the same time an SMS with a six-digit code arrives.
steps: She recognises the pattern: someone is trying to register HER number on another phone. Her cousin's account has probably already been hijacked.
She does not send the code and calls her cousin on a normal phone call. The cousin says she did not send the message.
Chioma opens Settings, Account, Two-step verification and turns it on with a new PIN and her email.
She warns her cousin to recover her account by verifying her number again and to report the problem to WhatsApp support from Settings, Help.
blocks.result: Chioma's account stays safe. With two-step verification on, the fraudster would need her PIN even if she had slipped and shared the code.

blocks.text: More locks you can use

items: **App lock:** use your fingerprint, face or phone passcode to open WhatsApp (in Privacy settings on Android, or Screen lock on iPhone).
**Chat lock:** lock one sensitive chat behind your fingerprint or passcode, so it is hidden from anyone who borrows your phone.
**Disappearing messages:** set new messages in a chat to vanish after 24 hours, 7 days or 90 days. Useful for private matters, but remember people can still screenshot.
**Blocked contacts:** a list of people you have blocked. They cannot call or message you.

takeaways: Set last seen, profile photo and status to My contacts or tighter.
Limit who can add you to groups to stop scam groups.
Two-step verification PIN plus email is your strongest protection.
Never share the SMS code or your PIN with anyone, ever.

activity.title: Lock down your account
steps: Run Privacy checkup in Settings, Privacy.
Set Groups to My contacts or My contacts except.
Turn on two-step verification with a new six-digit PIN and add your email.
Write the PIN on paper and keep it somewhere safe.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of the Two-step verification screen showing it is on (do not include the PIN).

lessons.title: Saving, organising and blocking contacts
objectives: Save contacts with clear names so you can find them quickly
Share your contact using a WhatsApp QR code
Pin, archive and mute chats to keep your chat list tidy
Block and report a number that harasses or tries to scam you

blocks.text: WhatsApp reads the contacts saved in your phone. When you save a number, WhatsApp shows that person's chats under the name you gave them. A tidy contact list saves you time every day, and it also decides who can see your status and your profile photo if you chose "My contacts" in the last lesson.

blocks.name: mobile-user
blocks.alt: A person scrolling through contacts on a phone
blocks.caption: Good names in your contact list make every later task faster.

blocks.text: Ways to add a contact

items: **From WhatsApp:** tap the new chat button, then New contact. Type the name and number with +234, then Save.
**From a chat with an unsaved number:** open the chat, tap the number at the top, then Add to contacts (or Save).
**By QR code:** in Settings, tap the small QR code icon beside your name. Others scan it with their WhatsApp camera to add you instantly. You can also tap Scan code to add someone else.

blocks.text: Naming contacts so you can find them

A list full of "Mummy", "Mummy 2" and "Customer" quickly becomes useless. Use a simple pattern: **first name, then what or where**. For business contacts, many traders add the town or the product. Your phone searches any part of the name, so typing "Lekki" will find everyone you saved with Lekki.

head: Instead of
Save as
Why
rows: You remember what she buys and where
Easy to search by trade or area

blocks.text: Keeping your chat list tidy

blocks.title: Deciding what to do with a chat
items: Important daily? Pin it
Noisy group? Mute it
Finished? Archive it
Harmful? Block and report
blocks.caption: Four quick actions keep your most important conversations at the top.

items: **Pin:** press and hold a chat, then tap the pin icon. You can pin up to three chats to the top, for example your husband, your main supplier and your business group.
**Mute:** press and hold, tap the mute (speaker) icon and choose 8 hours, 1 week or Always. You still get messages, but your phone stays quiet.
**Archive:** press and hold, then tap the archive box. The chat moves to the Archived folder at the top of your list. It is not deleted and you can open it any time.
**Mark as unread:** press and hold, then Mark as unread, to remind yourself to reply later.

blocks.title: Worked example: cleaning up 300 chats
blocks.context: For example, Halima runs a small kitchen in Kaduna selling meals to offices. Her chat list has over 300 chats, and she keeps missing orders.
steps: She pins her three busiest office customers so they stay at the top.
She mutes six family and alumni groups for Always and checks them in the evening.
She archives 150 old chats from last year's customers. They are still saved, just out of the way.
She renames 40 customer contacts using her pattern, for example "Musa Office Barnawa".
blocks.result: Now when she opens WhatsApp at 11am, the first five chats are the people most likely to order lunch, and she stops missing orders.

blocks.text: Blocking and reporting

If someone harasses you, sends you suspicious links or tries to scam you, open their chat, tap their name or number at the top, scroll down and tap **Block**. A blocked contact cannot message you, call you or see your updates. You can also tap **Report**. Reporting sends WhatsApp the most recent messages from that person so they can investigate the account. Blocking does not tell the person you blocked them, but they may notice that their messages show only one tick.

blocks.title: Unknown number messaging you?
blocks.text: When an unsaved number messages you for the first time, WhatsApp shows options to Block or Add to contacts, and often shows whether you share any groups. Read the first message carefully before replying, and do not open links from strangers.
Deleting a contact

To delete a contact, you remove it from your phone's contact list (or open the contact in WhatsApp and choose Edit, then Delete). The chat history stays until you delete the chat itself. Deleting a contact does not block them: they can still message you, and the chat will just show their number instead of a name.
Contacts on a shared or family phone

Many women share a phone with a spouse or children, or hand it to a child for games. If that is you, a few habits help. Use **App lock** or **Chat lock** for business chats so customers' details stay private. Do not save customers under pet names that could cause misunderstanding at home; a clear business name such as "Funmi Ankara Lekki" explains itself. If you change phones, your contacts are usually saved in your Google account (Android) or iCloud (iPhone), not inside WhatsApp, so check that contact syncing is switched on in your phone settings. Then a new phone brings back both your chats, from the WhatsApp backup, and the names, from your Google or iCloud contacts.

takeaways: Save contacts as first name plus trade or area.
Use your QR code to share your contact quickly at events.
Pin up to three chats, mute noisy groups and archive old chats.
Block and report anyone who harasses or tries to scam you.

activity.title: Tidy your contacts
steps: Rename at least 10 contacts using the first name plus trade or area pattern.
Pin your three most important chats.
Mute every group that interrupts your day and archive at least 20 old chats.
Open your QR code in Settings and practise sharing it with a friend.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of your chat list showing three pinned chats and an Archived folder.

lessons.title: Finding your way around the WhatsApp screens
objectives: Name the main tabs: Chats, Updates, Communities and Calls
Read message ticks to know whether a message was sent, delivered or read
Find Settings, Storage and data, and linked devices
Use WhatsApp on a laptop with WhatsApp Web or the desktop app

blocks.text: WhatsApp looks simple, but there is a lot packed into each screen. Once you know where things live, you stop wasting data and time searching. Menu positions are slightly different on Android and iPhone, and they move a little with updates, but the names stay the same.

blocks.name: mobile-interface
blocks.alt: A large phone screen with menus and icons
blocks.caption: Learn the four main tabs and you can find almost any feature.

blocks.text: The main tabs

head: Tab
What you find there
rows: All your one-to-one and group conversations, with a search bar and filters such as Unread and Groups
Status updates from your contacts, and Channels you follow
Communities you belong to, each grouping several related groups
Your call history, plus buttons to start voice or video calls

blocks.text: On Android, **Settings** is under the three dots at the top right. On iPhone, Settings is a tab at the bottom. In Settings you will find Account, Privacy, Chats, Notifications, **Storage and data**, Help, and **Linked devices**.
Reading the ticks

blocks.title: What the ticks next to your message mean
items: Clock: not yet sent
One grey tick: sent
Two grey ticks: delivered
Two blue ticks: read
blocks.caption: Ticks show how far your message has travelled, from your phone to being read.

blocks.text: A **clock** means the message has not left your phone, usually because you have no data or network. **One grey tick** means it reached WhatsApp but not the other phone, perhaps because it is off or offline, or because the person has blocked you. **Two grey ticks** mean it was delivered to their phone. **Two blue ticks** mean they opened the chat. In a group, ticks turn blue only when everyone has read it. Press and hold your message and tap **Info** to see exactly who read it and when. Remember: if someone has switched off read receipts, you will never see blue ticks from them.
Inside a chat

items: **Top bar:** the contact's name and photo. Tap it to see their info, shared media, and options like mute, disappearing messages and block. The phone and camera icons start calls.
**Typing box:** type a message, tap the emoji face for emojis, the paperclip or plus for files, photos, location, contact and polls, and the camera for a quick photo.
**Microphone:** hold to record a voice message. It turns into a send arrow once you type text.
**Search:** inside a chat, use Search to find an old message by a word, such as "address" or "account number".

blocks.text: Saving data with Storage and data

In Settings, **Storage and data** has three useful parts. **Manage storage** shows which chats take up the most space and lets you delete large videos you no longer need. **Media auto-download** lets you choose which files download by themselves on mobile data, on Wi-Fi or when roaming. **Use less data for calls** reduces the data voice and video calls use.

blocks.title: Worked example: stopping videos from eating your bundle
blocks.context: For example, Grace in Benin City buys a 1.5GB monthly bundle for about 1,000 naira (approximate, prices change). It finishes in ten days because of videos from her church and family groups.
steps: She opens Settings, Storage and data, Media auto-download.
Under When using mobile data, she ticks only Photos and unticks Audio, Videos and Documents.
Under When connected on Wi-Fi, she leaves everything ticked for when she is at the office.
In Manage storage she deletes 2GB of old forwarded videos and frees space on her phone.
blocks.result: Videos now show a download button and only download when she taps them. Her bundle lasts much longer.

blocks.text: WhatsApp on a laptop

If you type a lot, use WhatsApp on a computer. Open **web.whatsapp.com** in a browser or install the WhatsApp desktop app from the official site or app store. On your phone, open Settings (or the three dots), tap **Linked devices**, then **Link a device**, and scan the QR code on the computer screen. Your chats appear on the laptop. You can link up to four devices to one WhatsApp account, and they keep working for a while even if your phone goes offline.

blocks.title: Check your linked devices
blocks.text: Open Linked devices from time to time. If you see a computer or browser you do not recognise, tap it and choose Log out. Someone who briefly had your phone could have linked their laptop to read your messages.
Help and your own notes

Two more places are worth knowing. **Settings, Help** contains the Help Center, where WhatsApp explains each feature, and a Contact us option for reporting a problem. And at the top of your contact list you can choose **Message yourself**: a private chat with your own number. Use it as a notebook for things you want to keep handy, such as your account details to paste for customers, a draft message, a voice note to remember a task, or a document you want to open quickly on your laptop later.

takeaways: Main tabs: Chats, Updates, Communities, Calls; Settings holds everything else.
Clock, one grey, two grey, two blue: not sent, sent, delivered, read.
Media auto-download and Manage storage save data and space.
Link WhatsApp to a laptop with Linked devices, and log out devices you do not know.

activity.title: Explore and save data
steps: Open each of the four main tabs and write down one thing you found in each.
Set Media auto-download on mobile data to Photos only.
Use Manage storage to delete at least one large unwanted video.
Open Linked devices and confirm every device listed is yours.
activity.evidence: A short note listing the four tabs and a screenshot of your Media auto-download settings.

quiz.q: Ada receives an SMS with a six-digit WhatsApp code she did not request, followed by a message from a friend's account asking her to forward it. What should she do?
options: Send the code, because the friend made a mistake
Not share the code and turn on two-step verification
Reply asking the friend why they need it, then send it
quiz.explain: The code lets someone register Ada's number on another phone. WhatsApp never asks for it. Keeping it private and adding a two-step verification PIN protects the account.

quiz.q: Which setting stops strangers from adding you to investment and forex groups?
quiz.explain: In Settings, Privacy, Groups controls who can add you to groups. Setting it to My contacts or My contacts except blocks strangers.

quiz.q: Your message shows two grey ticks for an hour. What does that mean?
options: It was delivered but not yet opened, or the person has read receipts off
It was not sent because you have no data
quiz.explain: Two grey ticks mean delivered. They turn blue when read, unless read receipts are switched off on either side.

quiz.q: Kemi's bundle finishes quickly because group videos download by themselves. Where should she go?
options: Settings, Storage and data, Media auto-download
quiz.explain: Media auto-download controls which files download automatically on mobile data, Wi-Fi and roaming.

quiz.q: Which is the safest way to get WhatsApp on a new Android phone?
options: Install a file a friend sends on WhatsApp
Download GB WhatsApp for more features
Install from Google Play, developer WhatsApp LLC
Copy the app from the old phone by Bluetooth
quiz.explain: Only the official stores provide the genuine app. Modified versions can steal data and get accounts banned.

quiz.q: Ifeoma sees a browser she does not recognise in Linked devices. What should she do first?
options: Ignore it, it is probably WhatsApp testing
Tap it and log it out, then check two-step verification is on
quiz.explain: An unknown linked device may be someone reading her messages. Logging it out removes access immediately.

modules.title: Messaging, Calls, Media and Status
modules.overview: This module covers the everyday tools: writing clear messages, replying and forwarding wisely, voice notes and calls, sharing photos and documents without wasting data, and using Status to keep people informed. You will practise each one on your own phone.

lessons.title: Writing, replying, editing and forwarding messages
objectives: Reply to a specific message so your answer is never confused
Format text with bold, italics and lists to make messages easy to read
Edit or delete a message you sent by mistake
Recognise forwarded messages and check them before passing them on

blocks.text: Text messages are still the heart of WhatsApp. A clear message saves back-and-forth, shows respect and, in business, wins trust. This lesson shows you the tools that make messages clearer: replying to a specific message, simple formatting, editing, deleting, reacting and forwarding responsibly.

blocks.name: texting
blocks.alt: A woman typing a message on her phone
blocks.caption: Clear, well-formatted messages save time for you and the person reading.

blocks.text: Reply to the exact message

In a busy chat, "Yes" can mean anything. To reply to one message, **swipe it to the right** (or press and hold and tap Reply). The original message appears in a small box above your answer. This is called quoting. In groups, you can also press and hold and choose **Reply privately** to answer one person in a separate chat.
Format your text

head: Type this
You get
Use it for
rows: - item (dash and space at line start)

blocks.text: You can also press and hold on a word while typing, select it and choose Bold or Italic from the menu. Keep formatting light: one or two bold words stand out, but a whole message in bold feels like shouting.

blocks.title: Worked example: a clear order confirmation
blocks.context: For example, Amaka sells small chops in Port Harcourt. A customer asks for 50 packs for a birthday on Saturday.
steps: She swipes right on the customer's order message to reply to it directly.
She types: *Order confirmed* then a new line for each detail.

- 50 packs small chops at 1,500 naira each (approximate example price)
- Total: *75,000 naira*
- Delivery: Saturday, 11am, GRA Phase 2
She adds: Please pay 50% (37,500 naira) to confirm. Account details below.
blocks.result: The customer sees a neat summary with the total in bold and the exact order it answers. There are no follow-up questions, and the deposit arrives within the hour.

blocks.text: Editing and deleting

items: **Edit:** press and hold a message you sent and tap Edit. You can edit for up to 15 minutes after sending. The message then shows the word "Edited".

**Delete for everyone:** press and hold, tap Delete, then Delete for everyone. This only works for a limited time after sending, and the chat shows "This message was deleted". The other person may already have read it or seen it in a notification.
**Delete for me:** removes the message only from your phone.

blocks.title: Typed the wrong account number?
blocks.text: Edit it quickly rather than sending a second message, so nobody pays into the wrong account. Then send a short note: "Corrected account number above, please check."
Reactions, stars and pins

Press and hold a message to **react** with an emoji such as a thumbs-up. This is a quick way to say "seen, thank you" without adding another message. Tap the **star** to save important messages, like an address or a price, then find them later under Starred messages. In a chat or group you can also **pin** a message so it stays at the top, for example the delivery address or the meeting rules.
Forwarding responsibly

blocks.title: Before you forward anything
items: Who wrote it originally?
Is there a date?
Can I confirm elsewhere?
Could it frighten or harm?
Would I sign my name?
blocks.caption: If you cannot tick every box, do not forward the message.

blocks.text: Messages you forward show a small **Forwarded** label. If a message has been forwarded through a chain of five or more chats, it shows **Forwarded many times** with a double arrow, and WhatsApp limits it so it can only be forwarded to one chat at a time. That label is a warning sign: viral messages about free government grants, miracle cures, kidnapping alerts or bank closures are very often false. Check trusted news sources or official websites, such as a ministry's or bank's own page, before sharing.

blocks.title: Fake grant and recruitment messages
blocks.text: Messages offering free money, scholarships or jobs that ask you to click a link, fill in your BVN or bank details, or forward to ten groups are scams. Real programmes do not ask you to forward them to unlock a reward.
Polite, professional wording

Text has no tone of voice, so short messages can sound rude by accident. "Ok" or "Send money" may feel cold to the person reading. Start with a greeting, use the person's name, and end with a clear next step: "Good morning Mrs Bello. Your order is ready. Would you like delivery today or tomorrow?" Avoid writing whole sentences in capital letters, which reads as shouting, and avoid long chains of emojis in business chats. If a message upsets you, wait a few minutes before replying, or call instead. A calm reply protects relationships with customers, colleagues and family.

takeaways: Swipe right to reply to the exact message you mean.
Use *bold*, _italic_ and dash lists to make messages easy to scan.
You can edit within 15 minutes; delete for everyone only works for a limited time.
Treat Forwarded many times as a reason to check before sharing.

activity.title: Send a clear message
steps: Write an order confirmation or meeting reminder using bold for the key line and a dash list for details.
Send it to a friend or to your own number by using Message yourself.
Practise editing the message within 15 minutes.
Star the message so you can find it under Starred messages.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of your formatted message showing bold text and a list.

lessons.title: Voice notes, voice calls and video calls
objectives: Record, preview and send a clear voice message
Make one-to-one and group voice and video calls
Reduce the data a call uses
Choose when a voice note, call or text is the right tool

blocks.text: Voice is natural for many people, especially when typing is slow or when you speak more comfortably in Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo or Pidgin. WhatsApp gives you voice messages, voice calls and video calls, all over the internet. Used well, they save time. Used badly, a five-minute voice note can frustrate a busy customer.

blocks.name: voice-messages
blocks.alt: A person speaking into a phone with sound waves
blocks.caption: Voice notes are quick to record, but should be short and clear for the listener.

blocks.text: Recording a good voice message

items: Open the chat and **press and hold the microphone**. Speak, then let go to send.
For a longer message, **slide your finger up to the lock** so you can record without holding. Tap Stop to listen to it before sending.
If you make a mistake, slide left (or tap the bin) to cancel.
When listening to a long voice note someone sent you, tap **1x** to change to 1.5x or 2x speed.

blocks.title: The 60-second habit
blocks.text: Plan what you will say first: who you are, what you need, and the next step. Try to keep business voice notes under a minute. Put key details like amounts, dates and account numbers in text as well, because people cannot search inside a voice note.

You can also send a short **video message** in a chat: tap the microphone once to switch it to a camera icon, then hold to record. It is a quick way to show a customer a fabric or a finished cake without making a full video call.
Voice and video calls

Tap the **phone icon** at the top of a chat for a voice call, or the **camera icon** for a video call. For a group call, open the Calls tab, tap the button to start a new call and choose people, or start a call from inside a group. WhatsApp group calls allow **up to 32 people**. You can switch from voice to video during a call, mute your microphone, and use the speaker.

WhatsApp calls are protected by **end-to-end encryption**. This means only you and the people on the call can hear what is said, not WhatsApp and not anyone in between. It does not stop the other person recording, so speak as if a call could be repeated.
Which tool to use when

blocks.title: Choosing text, voice note or call
items: Voice call
Video call
Text message
Voice note
axes: Needs to be seen: no to yes
blocks.caption: Urgent things deserve a call; things to keep and search belong in text.

head: Situation
Best choice
Why
rows: Easy to copy and search later
Explaining feelings or a sensitive matter
Showing a product or checking a fitting
Instructions for someone who reads slowly
Voice note plus key numbers in text
Easy to listen to, details still saved

blocks.text: Saving data on calls

Video calls use much more data than voice calls. To reduce data, go to **Settings, Storage and data** and switch on **Use less data for calls**. Use Wi-Fi when you can, and switch off your camera if the picture is not needed. Before a long video meeting, check your bundle balance with your network's USSD code.

blocks.title: Worked example: a fitting by video call
blocks.context: For example, Zainab is a tailor in Kano. Her customer Hauwa lives in Abuja and wants to see her wedding outfit before it is sent.
steps: Zainab sends a text: "Your outfit is ready. Can I video call you at 4pm to show it?" so Hauwa can find good Wi-Fi.
At 4pm she starts a video call and shows the front, the back and the embroidery close up, with the outfit on a mannequin near a window for good light.
Hauwa asks for the sleeve to be shortened by 2cm. Zainab confirms it in text after the call: "Sleeve shortened 2cm, ready Friday."
She sends a 20-second video message of the finished sleeve on Friday.
blocks.result: Hauwa approves the outfit without travelling, and there is a written record of the change in the chat.

blocks.title: Unknown video calls
blocks.text: Do not answer video calls from unknown international numbers. Some scammers record the call or use it to blackmail. Silence unknown callers (Settings, Privacy, Calls) stops these calls from ringing.
Missed calls and call manners

Before calling someone you do not know well, especially a customer or official, send a short text first: "Good afternoon, this is Zainab the tailor. Is it a good time for a 5-minute call?" This respects their time and data. If you miss a call, the Calls tab shows it with a red arrow; tap the phone icon beside it to call back. If you cannot talk, decline the call and send a short text such as "Can't talk now, I will call you by 4pm", then keep that promise. In meetings, mute your microphone when you are not speaking so background noise does not disturb others.

takeaways: Hold the mic to record, slide up to lock, preview before sending.
Keep business voice notes short and put key numbers in text.
Group calls take up to 32 people; video uses much more data than voice.
Switch on Use less data for calls and silence unknown callers.

activity.title: Practise voice and calls
steps: Record a voice note under 60 seconds that says who you are, what you offer and how to order.
Lock the recording, listen to it, and re-record if it is unclear.
Make one video call to a friend and practise switching the camera and muting.
Switch on Use less data for calls.
activity.evidence: Your saved voice note (sent to Message yourself) and a written script of what you said.

lessons.title: Sharing photos, videos, documents and locations
objectives: Send photos and videos in standard or HD quality
Send files such as PDFs, price lists and receipts as documents
Share your current or live location safely
Use view once for private images and know its limits

blocks.text: WhatsApp is how many of us share product pictures, school fees receipts, CVs and directions. Each type of file has a best way to send it. Knowing the difference keeps your pictures sharp, your documents professional and your data bundle under control.

blocks.name: photo-sharing
blocks.alt: Two people sharing pictures between phones
blocks.caption: Choose the right way to send each file: photo, HD photo, document or location.

blocks.text: Photos and videos

Tap the **paperclip** (Android) or **plus** (iPhone), then Gallery or Photos, and choose up to several pictures at once. Before sending you can crop, add text, draw or add a caption. WhatsApp shrinks photos to save data. If quality matters, for example a product photo for a customer, tap the **HD** button at the top before sending. HD files are bigger and use more data, so use HD for product shots and standard for everyday pictures.
Documents

Choose **Document** to send PDFs, Word files, spreadsheets, price lists or receipts. WhatsApp allows documents of up to 2GB. A file sent as a document is not compressed, so it reaches the other person exactly as it left your phone. This is also a trick for photos: send a picture as a document when the receiver needs every detail, such as an architect's plan or a scanned certificate.
Scanning paper with your phone

On many phones you can choose Document, then Scan document (or use the camera's scan option, or the free Google Drive app's scan button) to photograph a paper and turn it into a clean PDF. This is much clearer than a tilted photo of a receipt on a table.
Sharing location

items: **Current location:** sends a pin of where you are now. Good for a dispatch rider looking for your shop.

**Live location:** shows your movement for a time you choose, such as 15 minutes, 1 hour or 8 hours. Useful when travelling at night so family can follow your journey. You can stop sharing at any time.
Only share location with people you trust. Never post your home location in a large group.

blocks.title: Worked example: sending a quotation professionally
blocks.context: For example, Esther runs an events decoration business in Enugu. A client asks for a quote for a 200-guest wedding.
steps: She types the quote in a free app such as Google Docs, with her business name, items and prices marked as quotation figures.
She saves it as a PDF named "Esther Decor Quote Okafor Wedding.pdf".
In the client's chat, she taps paperclip, Document, and selects the PDF.
She adds a short message: "Please find the quote attached. It is valid for 14 days." and sends three HD photos of a previous decoration.
blocks.result: The client receives a clear, named document that can be printed or shown to family, plus sharp photos of past work.

blocks.text: View once and private images

When you choose a photo or video, tap the small **1** icon to send it as **view once**. The receiver can open it one time, then it disappears from the chat, and they cannot forward or save it in WhatsApp. WhatsApp also blocks screenshots of view-once media, but it cannot stop someone taking a picture of the screen with another phone. So view once is for privacy, not for sending something you would never want shared.

blocks.title: Choosing how to send a file
items: Is it a paper or PDF?
Yes: send as Document
Photo for selling? HD
Private? View once
blocks.caption: A few seconds of choice gives sharper pictures, cleaner documents and better privacy.

blocks.title: Protect personal documents
blocks.text: Be careful sending copies of your NIN slip, passport, BVN details or bank statements. Send them only to people and organisations you have confirmed, and delete them from chats when no longer needed. Never send your card PIN, OTP or full card details on WhatsApp.
Keeping your phone from filling up

Every photo, video and voice note you receive is saved on your phone. On a phone with 32GB or 64GB of storage, busy groups can fill it within months, and a full phone becomes slow and stops taking photos. Each month, open **Settings, Storage and data, Manage storage**. It sorts files by size and shows forwarded files separately, so you can delete large forwarded videos quickly. You can also open a chat's info and select Media, links and docs to review what that chat has sent you. Before deleting business documents such as receipts and invoices, save the important ones to Google Drive or a computer so you keep a record.

takeaways: Use HD for product photos and standard for everyday pictures.
Send PDFs, price lists and scans as Documents (up to 2GB, no compression).
Share live location only with trusted people and for a set time.
View once helps privacy but cannot stop a photo of the screen.

activity.title: Send a professional file
steps: Create a simple price list or CV and save it as a PDF with a clear file name.
Send it to Message yourself as a Document.
Send one product or personal photo in HD and compare it with a standard one.
Share your live location with a trusted family member for 15 minutes, then stop it.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of the PDF you sent as a document, showing its file name.

lessons.title: Using WhatsApp Status to share updates
objectives: Post text, photo, video and voice status updates
Control exactly who can see your status
See who viewed your status and reply to others' updates
Plan a simple weekly status routine for your work or community

blocks.text: **Status** lets you post text, photos, videos, voice updates and links that **disappear after 24 hours**. Your contacts find them in the **Updates** tab. Many Nigerian traders call Status their free shop window: customers check it like a daily newspaper. It is also a gentle way to share family news without sending a message to everyone.

blocks.name: status-update
blocks.alt: A person posting an update on a phone screen
blocks.caption: Status updates last 24 hours and reach the contacts who have saved your number.

blocks.text: Who can see your status

A contact sees your status only if **you have saved their number and they have saved yours**. This is why traders ask customers, "Please save my number so you can see my status." Then you choose your audience in **Status privacy**, in the Updates tab menu or Settings, Privacy, Status:

items: **My contacts:** everyone saved in your phone (who has also saved you).
**My contacts except...:** everyone except people you pick, for example your boss or an ex.
**Only share with...:** only the people you pick, for example only your customers.

blocks.text: Posting a status

items: Open the Updates tab and tap the camera button to post a photo or video, or the pencil button to post text on a coloured background.
Add a caption, text or drawing. For text status you can change the font and the background colour.
Check the audience shown at the bottom, then tap Send.
To post a voice update, open the text status screen and hold the microphone.

blocks.text: Tap **My status** to see your updates. Swipe up (or tap the eye icon) to see **who viewed** each one. Read receipts affect this: if you switched off read receipts, you will not see your viewers, and others will not see that you viewed theirs. You can delete a status before the 24 hours end.
Replying and muting

When you watch someone's status, swipe up or tap **Reply** to send a private message about that update. The reply arrives in a normal chat with a small preview of the status. You can react quickly with an emoji too. If one contact posts too much, press and hold their status and tap **Mute**. Their updates move to the bottom and stop appearing first.
A simple weekly status plan

blocks.title: A weekly status rhythm for a small business
items: Monday: new stock
Wednesday: customer review
Friday: offer or deadline
Sunday: behind the scenes
blocks.caption: A steady rhythm keeps customers watching without flooding their screens.

blocks.title: Worked example: selling through Status
blocks.context: For example, Tola sells ready-made Ankara dresses in Akure. She has about 600 saved contacts and wants more sales without paying for adverts.
steps: On Monday she posts four HD photos of new dresses with price and sizes in the caption: "Size 12 to 16, 18,000 naira (approximate). Reply to order."
On Wednesday she posts a screenshot of a happy customer's message, with the customer's permission and their name hidden.
On Friday she posts: "Last 3 pieces at this price, offer ends Saturday 6pm."
She checks views each evening and replies to every status reply within an hour.
blocks.result: Customers reply directly to the dresses they like, which arrive in her chats with the photo attached, so she always knows which dress they mean.

blocks.title: Good status habits
blocks.text: Post a few strong updates a day rather than twenty. Use clear photos in daylight, put the price or key detail in the caption, and end with one action, such as Reply to order. Ask permission before posting other people's faces or messages.

blocks.title: Do not overshare
blocks.text: Status is short-lived but not private: anyone who can view it can screenshot it. Avoid posting your children's school uniform with the school name, your travel plans while you are away, or large amounts of cash and new purchases.

In the Updates tab you will also see **Channels**. Channels are different from Status: they are one-way broadcasts from organisations, brands and public figures that you choose to follow. You will learn about them in Module 3.
Making status content that people actually watch

People tap through status quickly, so each update must make sense in two or three seconds. Use one main idea per post. For photos, fill the frame with the product and shoot near a window or outside in daylight. For text status, use large, short sentences and strong contrast, such as white text on a dark colour. For videos, keep them short and show the product being used, such as a gown moving as someone walks. Put the price, size or date in the caption so people do not need to message you just to ask. Finally, mix selling with value: a cooking tip, a styling idea or a community notice keeps people watching, while nonstop adverts make them mute you.

items: Morning (about 7am to 9am) and evening (about 7pm to 9pm) are often busy times, but watch your own viewer counts to find your best times.
Post links to your catalogue or a product so customers can tap straight through.
Check how many people viewed each update to learn which kinds of posts your audience likes most.

takeaways: Status disappears after 24 hours and lives in the Updates tab.
Only contacts who saved your number, and whom you saved, can see it.
Use My contacts except or Only share with to control the audience.
Status replies arrive as private chats, ideal for orders and questions.

activity.title: Plan and post
steps: Check your Status privacy and choose the audience that suits you.
Write a four-day status plan for your work, church group or community project.
Post one text status and one photo status with a clear caption and one action.
After a few hours, check who viewed it and reply to any responses.
activity.evidence: Your written four-day plan and a screenshot of your status viewers list (blur names if you wish).

quiz.q: A customer says she cannot see Ngozi's status. What is the most likely reason?
options: The customer has not saved Ngozi's number, or Ngozi has not saved hers
Status only works on WhatsApp Business
quiz.explain: Status is visible only when both people have saved each other's numbers, and only for 24 hours.

quiz.q: Bunmi typed the wrong account number in a message two minutes ago. What is the best action?
options: Send a new message saying sorry
Leave it, the customer will ask
Edit the message and send a short note pointing to the correction
quiz.explain: Messages can be edited for up to 15 minutes. Editing prevents payment to the wrong account.

quiz.q: Which is the best way to send a price list so it looks professional and is not compressed?
quiz.explain: Documents are sent without compression and can be opened, saved and printed.

quiz.q: A message about a free federal grant shows Forwarded many times and asks for your BVN. What should you do?
options: Forward it to your groups so others benefit
Fill in your BVN quickly before it closes
Reply to ask the sender if it is real
Do not share it or give details, and check official sources
quiz.explain: Forwarded many times signals a viral chain. Requests for BVN or bank details through forwarded links are a classic scam.

quiz.q: Which call setting reduces the data used by WhatsApp calls?
options: Use less data for calls in Storage and data
quiz.explain: Use less data for calls, under Settings, Storage and data, lowers call data use.

quiz.q: Rukayat wants only her customers, not her family, to see her product updates. Which status setting fits?
options: Only share with, choosing her customers
quiz.explain: Only share with lets her pick exactly who sees her status.

modules.title: Groups, Channels, Broadcast Lists and Communities
modules.overview: Here you learn to reach many people at once in the right way: groups for conversation, broadcast lists for private one-to-many messages, channels for public announcements and communities for organising many groups. You will also learn the etiquette and notification settings that keep groups useful instead of exhausting.

lessons.title: Creating and running a WhatsApp group as an admin
objectives: Create a group with a clear name, photo and description
Add members by contact or by invite link, and reset a leaked link
Use group settings to control who can post, edit and join
Share admin duties and remove members respectfully

blocks.text: A WhatsApp group lets everyone in it see and reply to every message. A group can hold **up to 1,024 members**. Groups are good for teams, cooperatives, church departments, school parents and customer clubs, where people need to talk to each other. The person who creates the group is the first **admin**, and admins control the settings.

blocks.name: group-chat
blocks.alt: Several people chatting together in a group conversation
blocks.caption: A well-run group has a clear purpose, simple rules and active admins.

blocks.text: Creating a group

items: In the Chats tab, tap the new chat button, then **New group**.
Select the contacts you want to add, then tap the arrow.
Type a **group name** that says what it is for, such as "Ikeja Women Traders Cooperative" rather than "Our Family 2".
Add a **group photo**, then tap Create.
Open the group info and write a **description** with the purpose and three or four rules.

blocks.text: Inviting with a link

In group info, tap **Invite via link** (or Invite to group via link). You can copy the link, share it, or show a **QR code** for people to scan at a meeting. Anyone with the link can join, so share it carefully. If the link gets into the wrong hands, tap **Reset link**: the old link stops working and a new one is created.
Group settings every admin should know

head: Setting
What it does
When to use it
rows: Choose whether all members or only admins can change the name, photo and description
Set to admins only to stop pranks
Choose whether all members or only admins can post
Admins only for an announcements group
Admins must approve anyone joining through the link
Large or public groups, to keep out strangers
New messages vanish after 24 hours, 7 days or 90 days
Groups that do not need a long record

blocks.text: Admins can also **delete a member's message for everyone**, for example a scam link or an offensive post. The chat shows that an admin deleted it. To make someone an admin, open group info, tap their name and choose **Make group admin**. To remove a member, tap their name and choose **Remove**.

blocks.title: Layers of a healthy group
items: Active admins
Clear rules in description
Right settings
Clear purpose and name
blocks.caption: Start from the base: a clear purpose, then settings, rules and admins who act.

blocks.title: Worked example: setting up a cooperative group
blocks.context: For example, Mama Funke chairs a 60-member women's thrift cooperative (ajo) in Ibadan. Their old group was full of forwarded videos and members missed contribution reminders.
steps: She creates a new group named "Bodija Women Ajo 2026" with the cooperative's logo.
Description: "For contributions, meetings and loans only. No forwards, no adverts. Contributions due every Friday. Admins: Funke, Bola, Grace."
She sets Edit group settings to admins only and turns on Approve new members.
She makes the treasurer and secretary admins so three people share the work.
She pins the message with the payment account details and reminds members to always confirm the account with the treasurer by phone before paying.
blocks.result: The group stays focused on contributions, and new members are approved before they can see financial messages.

blocks.title: Money in groups
blocks.text: Scammers sometimes copy an admin's name and photo, then message members privately asking for payments to a new account. Tell members that account details will never change by private message, and pin that warning in the group.
Leaving or closing a group

Anyone can tap **Exit group** in group info. Only admins see who left. If a group has finished its purpose, for example a wedding committee after the wedding, the admin can set Send messages to admins only, post a thank-you note, and remove members, then exit. Members keep their copy of the chat history until they delete it.
Writing good group rules

Rules work best when they are few, specific and written in the description where every new member sees them. Aim for three to five rules. Say what the group is for, what is not allowed, and what happens when rules are broken. For example: "1. For cooperative business only. 2. No forwarded videos or adverts. 3. Contributions are confirmed only by the treasurer. 4. Members who break rules twice will be removed." Then apply the rules fairly, including to friends and older members. If you add a new rule, announce it in the group and update the description at the same time.

items: Use the group description for rules and the pinned message for the most urgent current notice.
Use **Message info** on an important announcement to see how many members have read it.
Give new members a short welcome message that points them to the description.
Review your admin list every few months: remove admins who are no longer active and thank them, so only people who are actually managing the group hold admin powers.

takeaways: Groups hold up to 1,024 members; admins control the settings.
Give the group a clear name, photo, description and rules.
Use admins-only editing, Approve new members and Reset link to stay in control.
Share admin duties and pin key information, including payment warnings.

activity.title: Set up a practice group
steps: Create a small group with two or three trusted friends or family members.
Add a clear name, photo and a description with three rules.
Set Edit group settings to admins only and turn on Approve new members.
Create an invite link, then reset it, and make one friend an admin.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of your group info showing the description and settings.

lessons.title: Broadcast lists and Channels: reaching many people
objectives: Explain how a broadcast list differs from a group
Create a broadcast list and know why some people do not receive it
Follow a channel and understand what channel admins can and cannot see
Choose between a group, broadcast list and channel for a given purpose

blocks.text: Sometimes you want to send the same message to many people without them seeing each other or replying to everyone. WhatsApp gives you two tools for this: **broadcast lists**, which send private copies to your contacts, and **Channels**, which let anyone follow your public updates.

blocks.name: broadcast
blocks.alt: A person sending one message out to many people
blocks.caption: Broadcast lists and channels send one message to many people without a noisy group.

blocks.text: Broadcast lists

A broadcast list is a saved list of contacts. When you send a message to it, **each person receives it as a normal private message from you**. They do not see the other people on the list, and when they reply, the reply comes only to you, in your private chat with them. A list can have **up to 256 contacts**, and you can make several lists.

blocks.title: The rule that confuses everyone
blocks.text: Only people who have **saved your number in their phone** will receive your broadcast messages. If a customer has not saved you, your broadcast simply does not reach them. Always ask new customers to save your number.

items: On Android, tap the three dots in the Chats tab and choose **New broadcast**. On iPhone, open Chats, then Broadcast lists, then New list. (In WhatsApp Business, look for broadcast options under Business tools, as menus there are changing.)
Select the contacts and tap the tick or Create.
Rename the list from its info screen, for example "Lagos customers" or "Choir members".
Type your message and send. It arrives in each person's private chat.

blocks.text: Channels

**Channels** are found in the Updates tab. A channel is a one-way tool for sending updates to a large audience: news organisations, football clubs, churches, government agencies and businesses use them. Followers can read, react with emojis and vote in polls, but they cannot reply in the channel. Importantly, **followers cannot see the admin's phone number, and admins cannot see followers' phone numbers**. That privacy makes channels safer for public announcements than a huge group.

To follow a channel, open Updates, tap Find channels or search, and tap Follow. To create your own channel, tap the plus button in the Channels section and choose Create channel, then add a name, description and picture. Share the channel link on your status, flyers or social media so people can follow it.
Choosing the right tool

blocks.title: Broadcast list versus channel
items: Broadcast list
Channel
blocks.caption: Use broadcast lists for people you know personally and channels for public updates.

head: Your goal
Best tool
rows: Members need to discuss and decide together
Send a private price update to 150 regular customers
Share weekly health tips with the whole town
Remind 40 parents about a meeting without exposing their numbers to each other

blocks.title: Worked example: a price update without a noisy group
blocks.context: For example, Uche sells foodstuff in bulk in Onitsha. Prices of rice and beans change often, and she has about 400 regular buyers.
steps: She divides her buyers into two broadcast lists: "Retailers A to L" (200 contacts) and "Retailers M to Z" (200 contacts), each under the 256 limit.
She asks every buyer to save her number, and puts a notice on her stall: "Save 0803 to get weekly prices."
Every Monday she sends: *This week's prices* with a short list, marked "approximate, call to confirm".
Replies arrive privately, so she takes orders one by one without 400 people seeing each other's numbers.
blocks.result: Buyers get prices like a personal message, nobody's number is exposed, and there is no group arguing about prices.

blocks.title: Respect people's time
blocks.text: Do not broadcast every day. Once or twice a week with genuinely useful information keeps people from muting or blocking you. If someone asks to be removed, remove them from the list straight away.
Running your own channel well

If you create a channel, treat it like a small newsletter. Post on a regular schedule, for example three times a week, so followers know what to expect. Each post can be text, a photo, a video, a voice message, a link or a **poll**, and followers can react with emojis, which tells you what they find useful. Channel updates are kept for a limited time rather than forever, so put long-term information, such as your address or opening hours, in the channel description. As admin you can also invite other trusted people to help post. Promote the channel link on your status, at events and on printed flyers.

Remember that a channel is public. Anyone who finds the link can follow it and read what you post, so never share members' names, phone numbers, photos of children or private matters there. Use a group or a private chat for anything personal.

takeaways: Broadcast lists send private copies; replies come only to you.
A list holds up to 256 contacts, and only people who saved your number receive it.
Channels are one-way, public, and hide phone numbers on both sides.
Pick group for discussion, broadcast for known contacts, channel for the public.

activity.title: Build a broadcast list
steps: Create a broadcast list of five to ten contacts who have saved your number.
Name it clearly and send one useful message, such as a meeting reminder or price list.
Follow two channels relevant to your work or community, such as a news or health channel.
Write one sentence on which tool you would use for your main audience and why.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of your broadcast list info screen and your one-sentence decision.

lessons.title: WhatsApp Communities: organising many groups under one roof
objectives: Explain what a community is and how its announcement group works
Create a community and add existing or new groups to it
Decide when an organisation needs a community instead of one big group
Manage community admin and member privacy

blocks.text: As an organisation grows, it usually ends up with many groups: one for leaders, one for each branch, one for each project. Members join some groups and not others, and important announcements get lost. **WhatsApp Communities** solve this by putting related groups under one community, with one **announcement group** that reaches every member.

blocks.name: online-community
blocks.alt: People connected together in an online network
blocks.caption: A community links related groups and gives leaders one place for announcements.

blocks.text: How a community is built

blocks.title: The shape of a WhatsApp community
items: Community admins
Announcement group
Linked groups
Members
blocks.caption: Admins post once in the announcement group and it reaches members of every linked group.

items: **Community:** the container, with a name, photo and description.
**Announcement group:** created automatically. Every member of the community is in it, and normally only community admins can post there.
**Groups:** the normal groups linked to the community, such as branches or departments. Members can see the list of groups and ask to join those they need.
**Community admins:** manage the community, add or remove groups and send announcements. Each group still has its own group admins.

blocks.text: Creating a community

items: Open the **Communities** tab (on some Android phones it is the people icon) and tap New community, then Get started.
Enter a community name, description and photo. The description should say who it is for and what the announcement group will be used for.
Tap to add groups: either **Add existing groups** you already admin, or **Create new group**.
Tap Create. WhatsApp sets up the announcement group automatically.
Invite members with the community invite link, or members of linked groups become community members automatically.

blocks.text: **Privacy in communities:** members of the community do not see the phone numbers of everyone in the community. They see numbers only of people in the same groups as them, and admins' numbers. This protects members in large organisations where not everyone knows each other.
Community or one big group?

head: Situation
Better choice
rows: A 25-person family or committee who all talk to each other
A women's network with branches in several towns
Community with a group per branch
A school with parents in different classes
Community with a group per class
A business with customers only receiving news

blocks.title: Worked example: a women's network with branches
blocks.context: For example, Agnes coordinates a women's empowerment network with branches in Jos, Bauchi and Gombe. She manages seven separate groups and keeps copying announcements into each one.
steps: She creates a community called "Northern Women Network" with the description: "Announcements for all members. Branch chat happens in branch groups."
She adds her existing groups: Jos branch, Bauchi branch, Gombe branch, Leaders, Tailoring project, Farming project and Finance committee.
She makes two branch coordinators community admins so they can also post announcements.
She posts the monthly meeting notice once in the announcement group instead of seven times.
Members of the Jos branch can see that a Tailoring project group exists and request to join it.
blocks.result: Announcements go out once and reach everyone. Branch groups stay for local chat, and members discover projects they may want to join.

blocks.title: Keep the announcement group calm
blocks.text: Post announcements only: meetings, deadlines, important decisions. Keep discussion in the linked groups. A short, regular update, such as one every week, works better than many messages a day.

blocks.title: Limits change
blocks.text: WhatsApp sets limits on how many groups a community can hold and how many members its announcement group can have, and has raised these limits over time. Check the WhatsApp Help Center for the current numbers before planning a very large community.
Running a community day to day

A community needs a small team. Choose two or three **community admins** who post announcements and add or remove groups, and let each linked group keep its own **group admins** who manage local discussion. Agree in advance who writes announcements, and how often. A simple plan works: one weekly announcement every Monday with meetings, deadlines and decisions, and urgent notices only when something truly cannot wait.

Members can **exit a community** from the community info screen. Admins can remove a group from the community without deleting the group itself; the group simply becomes a normal group again. If someone breaks the rules in the announcement group replies or in a linked group, community admins can remove them from the community. Review the list of linked groups every few months and remove groups that are no longer active, so members see only what is useful.

items: Write the purpose of every linked group in its description so members know which ones to join.
Use the announcement group for events, deadlines and decisions, not for debate.
Keep a written list of community admins and group admins, with their phone numbers, for the leadership team.

takeaways: A community links related groups with one announcement group for everyone.
Community admins post announcements; group admins still run each group.
Members see numbers only of people in the same groups and of admins.
Use a community when an organisation has several branches or departments.

activity.title: Design a community
steps: Pick an organisation you belong to, such as a church, cooperative or alumni association.
Draw on paper the community name, the announcement group and three to six linked groups.
Write the community description in two sentences.
If you admin real groups and the leaders agree, create the community and add them.
activity.evidence: A photo of your community drawing and description, or a screenshot of the community you created.

lessons.title: Group etiquette, polls and controlling notifications
objectives: Follow and teach simple group etiquette rules
Use mentions and polls to get answers quickly in groups
Mute groups and set custom notifications to protect your time
Handle conflict and misinformation in a group calmly

blocks.text: Many of us belong to 30 or more groups: family, church, school, alumni, market, work. Without good habits, the phone buzzes all day and important messages are lost. This lesson covers how to behave well in groups, how to get decisions made, and how to take back control of your notifications.

blocks.name: notifications
blocks.alt: A phone showing many notification alerts
blocks.caption: Good etiquette and smart notification settings make groups useful again.

blocks.text: Simple etiquette for everyone

items: Stay on the group's purpose. Post adverts only where the rules allow them.
Use **Reply** (swipe right) so people know which message you are answering.
Send one complete message instead of five short ones.
Do not forward unverified news, especially health, security or money alerts.
Respect quiet hours. Avoid posting between about 10pm and 6am except in emergencies.
Move private matters to a private chat with **Reply privately**.
Ask before adding someone to a group, and ask before posting their photo or number.

blocks.text: Mentions and polls

Type **@** followed by a name to **mention** someone in a group. They get a notification even if they muted the group, so use it only when you really need that person, for example to ask the treasurer to confirm a payment or to give a member a task with a deadline.

To make a decision, create a **poll**. Tap the paperclip or plus, choose **Poll**, type the question and options, and choose whether people can pick more than one answer. Members vote with a tap, and everyone sees the results update. Polls stop 50 people from typing "Saturday" and "Sunday" one after another.

blocks.title: Worked example: choosing a meeting date with a poll
blocks.context: For example, Precious is secretary of a 90-member alumni association in Calabar. Last time, choosing a date for the reunion took three days of messages.
steps: She creates a poll: "Which date works for the reunion planning meeting?"
Options: Saturday 7 Nov, 4pm; Sunday 8 Nov, 3pm; Saturday 14 Nov, 4pm. She allows multiple answers.
She pins the poll and mentions the five executive members with @ to vote first.
After 48 hours, the results show 52 votes for Saturday 14 Nov. She announces the date and closes the discussion.
blocks.result: The decision takes two days with almost no extra messages, and everyone can see that the majority chose the date.

blocks.text: Taking control of notifications

blocks.title: How to set notifications for each group
items: Keep alerts on
Custom: no sound, mentions only
Mute 8 hours
Mute always, check weekly
axes: Messages per day: few to many
blocks.caption: Important, quiet groups keep alerts; busy, low-value groups are muted.

items: **Mute:** press and hold a group, tap the mute icon, choose 8 hours, 1 week or Always.
**Custom notifications:** open group info, Notifications (or Custom notifications), and choose a different tone or no pop-up for that group, so you can recognise your business group by sound.
**Filters:** use the Unread or Groups filters at the top of Chats to catch up quickly.
**Archive:** archived chats stay hidden even when new messages arrive, if you keep the archive setting on.

blocks.text: Handling conflict and false information

When a quarrel starts in a group, an admin should step in early and calmly: remind everyone of the rules, ask the people involved to continue privately, and if needed set **Send messages** to admins only for a few hours to let tempers cool. When someone posts false information, reply to that message with a polite correction and a link to a trusted source, and an admin can delete it for everyone if it is harmful. Avoid public shaming: the goal is a group people want to stay in.

blocks.title: A five-minute group clean-up
blocks.text: Once a month, open your chat list and ask of each group: do I still need this? Exit groups that no longer serve you. Leaving politely is fine: a short "Thank you all, I am exiting to reduce my groups" is enough.
Being a good group member, not only a good admin

Etiquette is not only for admins. Before posting, ask: is this useful to most people here, or only to one person? Birthday wishes, prayers and greetings are welcome in many family and church groups, but in a work or cooperative group a simple reaction or a private message may be better. Read back through recent messages before asking a question, because the answer may already be there or in the pinned message. If you post a mistake, correct it quickly with Edit rather than adding several new messages. And when you leave a group, do it quietly or with one short thank-you note, never with an angry message.

Group chats can also be a place for **voice notes** that are too long. If you must send a voice note to a group, keep it under a minute and add a one-line text summary so members who cannot listen right away still get the point.

takeaways: Stay on purpose, reply to the exact message and respect quiet hours.
Use @mentions sparingly and polls for decisions.
Mute busy low-value groups; use custom notifications for important ones.
Admins calm conflict early and correct false information politely.

activity.title: Reclaim your notifications
steps: List all your groups and mark each as important or low value, busy or quiet.
Mute at least five busy, low-value groups.
Set a custom notification tone for your most important group.
Create a poll in your practice group to choose a date or option.
activity.evidence: Your group list with the marks you gave each one, and a screenshot of your poll.

quiz.q: Uche sends a broadcast to 200 customers, but one regular customer says she never got it. What is the most likely reason?
options: The customer has not saved Uche's number
quiz.explain: Only contacts who have saved your number receive broadcast messages.

quiz.q: A network has branches in four towns and leaders keep copying announcements into each group. What should they set up?
options: A community with each branch group linked
A larger group with all 1,500 members
quiz.explain: A community links the branch groups, and one post in the announcement group reaches all members.

quiz.q: An invite link to the cooperative group was posted on a public Facebook page. What should the admin do?
options: Reset the invite link and turn on Approve new members
quiz.explain: Resetting the link makes the old one stop working. Approving new members keeps strangers out.

quiz.q: Which statement about Channels is correct?
options: Followers can reply in the channel like a group
Admins can see all followers' phone numbers
Channels appear in the Calls tab
Followers and admins cannot see each other's phone numbers
quiz.explain: Channels are one-way and protect phone numbers on both sides. They live in the Updates tab.

quiz.q: A 90-member group needs to choose a meeting date quickly. What is the best tool?
options: A voice note asking everyone to reply
quiz.explain: A poll collects votes with one tap and shows live results, avoiding dozens of messages.

quiz.q: Two members start quarrelling loudly in a group. What should the admin do first?
options: Calmly remind everyone of the rules and ask them to continue privately
Post screenshots of the quarrel on Status
quiz.explain: Early, calm intervention protects the group. Admins-only messaging for a short time is the next step if needed.

modules.title: WhatsApp Business: Selling, Serving and Staying Safe
modules.overview: This module turns WhatsApp into a small business tool. You will set up the WhatsApp Business app and a complete business profile, build a catalogue, automate greetings and away messages, speed up replies with quick replies and labels, and protect your customers and yourself from common scams.

lessons.title: Getting started with the WhatsApp Business app
objectives: List the main tools the WhatsApp Business app adds
Decide which number to use and how to move from the personal app safely
Find the Business tools menu
Create a short link and QR code customers can use to chat with you

blocks.text: **WhatsApp Business** is a free app from WhatsApp made for small businesses: a hairdresser, a caterer, a tailor, a pharmacy, a school or a shop. It works like ordinary WhatsApp, so your customers use their normal WhatsApp to chat with you. The difference is on your side: you get tools to look professional, answer faster and keep track of orders.

blocks.name: business-chat
blocks.alt: A business owner chatting with a customer on a phone
blocks.caption: WhatsApp Business adds selling and customer service tools on top of normal chat.

blocks.text: What the Business app adds
