head: Tool
What it does
rows: Shows your business name, category, description, address, hours, email and website
A mobile shop window of products or services with photos and prices
Automatic welcome sent to new customers
Automatic reply when you are closed or busy
Saved answers you send with a shortcut
Colour tags to organise chats, such as New order or Paid
Let customers start a chat with you in one tap or scan

blocks.text: WhatsApp also lists features such as linking **up to 10 devices and agents** to one business account, so a shop assistant can reply from another phone or laptop, and a paid **Meta Verified** subscription that adds a verified badge and impersonation protection for businesses that qualify. You do not need these to start.
Which number to use

blocks.title: Choosing your business number
items: Business already on personal WhatsApp?
Yes: move that number
No: get a new SIM
Install WhatsApp Business
blocks.caption: Customers who already know your number should not lose you, so think before you switch.

items: **Use a separate business SIM** if you can. You keep family chats in personal WhatsApp and customers in WhatsApp Business, on the same dual-SIM phone.
**Move your existing number** if customers already know it. When you install WhatsApp Business and verify the same number, the app offers to move your chats across. Back up first.
A business account can also be registered on a **landline** number by choosing to verify with a phone call.

blocks.text: Installing and finding Business tools

items: Install **WhatsApp Business** from Play Store or App Store (developer WhatsApp LLC). It has a green icon with a B.
Verify your number with the six-digit SMS code.
Enter your **business name** exactly as customers know it, choose a **category** such as Clothing or Food and grocery, and add a logo.
Find **Business tools**: on Android tap the three dots, then Business tools; on iPhone tap Settings, then Business tools. Every feature in this module lives there.
Turn on two-step verification at once (Settings, Account). A business account is a valuable target for fraudsters.

blocks.text: Your short link and QR code

In Business tools, open **Short link** (on some versions it is inside Business profile or Share options). WhatsApp creates a link in the form **wa.me/** followed by your number in international format without the plus or the first zero, for example wa.me/2348031234567. Anyone who taps it opens a chat with you. You can also add a default message, such as "Hello, I want to order", that appears ready for the customer to send. The **QR code** does the same when scanned.

blocks.title: Worked example: putting your chat link everywhere
blocks.context: For example, Nkechi runs a small pharmacy and provisions shop in Aba and has just installed WhatsApp Business on a new MTN line, 0816 555 0123.
steps: Her short link becomes wa.me/2348165550123, because she drops the 0 and adds 234.
She sets the default message to "Hello Nkechi Pharmacy, I want to ask about...".
She prints the QR code on an A4 sheet and tapes it by the counter with the words "Scan to order on WhatsApp".
She adds the short link to her Instagram bio and her Facebook page button.
blocks.result: Within a month, customers order refills by WhatsApp before coming, and Nkechi prepares their bags in advance.

blocks.title: Business tools are free
blocks.text: Installing WhatsApp Business and using the profile, catalogue, greeting, away messages, quick replies and labels costs nothing beyond your data. Be careful of people selling "WhatsApp Business activation" or "blue tick" services: these are not from WhatsApp.
Personal app or Business app: common questions

items: **Can customers tell I use WhatsApp Business?** Yes, your chats show a business account, and customers can tap your name to see your business profile.
**Do I lose my chats when I switch?** If you back up first and verify the same number, WhatsApp offers to move your chat history into the Business app.
**Can my staff use the same account?** Yes, through Linked devices, so customers always message one number while more than one person replies.
**Will my customers pay anything?** No. They chat with you from their normal WhatsApp, using only their own data.

blocks.text: Before switching an existing number to WhatsApp Business, tell your regular contacts that your chats will now show a business profile, so nobody is confused. If the number is very personal, such as one your extended family uses, a new business SIM is usually the cleaner choice: your family chats stay private and your business number can be printed on flyers without worry.

takeaways: WhatsApp Business is free and customers chat with you on normal WhatsApp.
Use a separate business SIM, or move your existing number after a backup.
Every business feature lives under Business tools.
Share your wa.me short link and QR code wherever customers see you.

activity.title: Launch your business account
steps: Install WhatsApp Business with the number you choose and verify it.
Add your business name, category and logo.
Turn on two-step verification.
Create your short link with a default message and save the QR code image.
activity.evidence: Your wa.me short link written down and the saved QR code image.

lessons.title: Building a complete, trustworthy business profile
objectives: Fill in every field of the business profile accurately
Write a short description that tells customers what you sell and where
Set business hours that match your away message
Check your profile as a customer sees it

blocks.text: Your **business profile** is what a customer sees when she taps your name in a chat. It answers the questions every new customer has: Who are you? What do you sell? Where are you? When are you open? How else can I reach you? A complete profile builds trust before you have typed a word.

blocks.name: online-profile
blocks.alt: A profile card with a photo and details
blocks.caption: A complete business profile answers a new customer's first questions for you.

blocks.text: The fields to fill
Open **Business tools, Business profile** (or Settings, then tap your business name). You will see these fields:

head: Field
What to write
Example
rows: Your logo, or a clear photo of you or your shop front
The closest match from WhatsApp's list
What you sell, for whom, and where, in one or two lines
Home-style Nigerian meals for offices in Victoria Island. Order by 10am for lunch delivery.
Working contacts only; Instagram or Facebook links can go in the website fields

blocks.text: Writing a description that sells

Use a simple formula: **what you offer + who it is for + where or how + one action**. Keep it short: customers read it on a small screen. Avoid vague words like "quality" and "affordable" on their own. Say something specific instead, such as "NAFDAC-registered" (only if your product truly is), "same-day delivery in Wuse", or "sizes 8 to 22".

blocks.title: Is your profile complete?
items: Clear logo or photo
Exact business name
Specific description
Address or landmark
Real business hours
Working email or link
blocks.caption: Tick all six before you share your link with customers.

blocks.title: Worked example: improving a weak profile
blocks.context: For example, Blessing makes and sells shea butter body creams in Abuja. Her first profile said only: "Blessing Cosmetics. Quality products at affordable prices."
steps: She changes the photo from a selfie to her logo on a white background.
She picks the category Beauty, cosmetic and personal care.
New description: "Handmade shea butter creams for dry skin, 250g and 500g jars. Delivery in Abuja, waybill nationwide. Tap Catalog to order."
She adds her workshop landmark in Kubwa, hours Mon to Sat 9am to 5pm, her Gmail and her Instagram link.
She asks a friend to tap her name in a chat and send a screenshot of what they see.
blocks.result: New customers now ask about specific jar sizes instead of "What do you sell?", and her conversations start closer to a sale.

blocks.text: Business hours and away messages work together

When you set business hours, customers can see whether you are open now. In the next lesson you will set an **away message** that can be sent automatically **outside of business hours**. That option uses the hours you enter here, so make them accurate. If you close for a holiday, update your hours or use a custom away message.

blocks.title: Be truthful in your profile
blocks.text: Do not claim registrations, awards or certifications you do not have, such as NAFDAC or SON approval, or CAC registration. Customers increasingly check, and false claims can bring legal trouble as well as lost trust. If you are registered, you can mention your registration accurately.
Seeing your profile as a customer does

Send a message from your business number to a friend, then ask them to tap your business name at the top of the chat. They will see your photo, description, hours, address and catalogue preview. Ask them two questions: "Do you know what I sell?" and "Do you know how to order?" If either answer is no, rewrite the description.
Keeping your profile current

A profile is not set once and forgotten. Each time something changes, update it the same day: a new shop address, new opening hours, a new phone line, a seasonal product, or closure for a holiday such as Christmas or Sallah. An out-of-date address sends a dispatch rider to the wrong place, and out-of-date hours make customers think you ignored them. A useful habit is to check your profile on the first day of every month together with your catalogue prices.

Use the same **name and logo** across WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and printed materials. Customers recognise you faster, and it is harder for impersonators to confuse them. If you notice another account using your name or logo, tell your customers on Status that you only use your own number, report the account to WhatsApp from its chat, and keep your own profile complete and consistent so the genuine account is easy to spot.

items: Logo: square, simple, readable when small.
Category: pick the one customers would search for.
Links: put your strongest page first, such as Instagram if that is where your reviews are.

takeaways: Fill every field: photo, name, category, description, address, hours, email and links.
Description formula: what, for whom, where or how, one action.
Accurate business hours power the outside-hours away message.
Never claim registrations or approvals you do not hold.

activity.title: Complete your profile
steps: Fill in every business profile field.
Write your description using the formula and keep it under about 30 words.
Set your real business hours.
Ask a friend to check your profile and answer the two questions.
activity.evidence: A screenshot of your business profile as your friend sees it.

lessons.title: Catalogue, greeting and away messages, quick replies and labels
objectives: Add products or services to your catalogue with photos, prices and descriptions
Set a greeting message and an away message with the right schedule and audience
Create quick replies with shortcuts for your most common answers
Use labels to track every order from new customer to complete

blocks.text: These four tools are the engine of WhatsApp Business. The **catalogue** shows what you sell. **Greeting and away messages** answer automatically. **Quick replies** save you typing the same thing fifty times. **Labels** make sure no order is forgotten. All four are in **Business tools**.

blocks.name: online-shopping
blocks.alt: A customer browsing products on a phone shop
blocks.caption: Your catalogue is a shop window customers can browse inside WhatsApp.

blocks.text: 1. The catalogue

items: Open Business tools, **Catalog**, then Add new item.
Add clear photos (daylight, plain background, several angles).
Enter the item name, price (optional), a description with size, colour or what is included, and optionally a link and an item code.
Save. Group items into **collections**, such as "Ankara gowns" and "Adire tops", to make browsing easy.
Share an item or the whole catalogue in a chat with the attach or catalogue button, or copy the catalogue link to your status and social media.

blocks.text: Customers can add items to a **cart** and send it to you as an order message. Prices change often, so update them regularly or write "Price on request" in the description for items with unstable prices.
2. Greeting and away messages

A **greeting message** is sent automatically when a customer messages you for the first time, or after 14 days with no messages between you. An **away message** is sent automatically when you cannot reply. For each, you choose the **recipients**: Everyone, Everyone not in address book, Everyone except, or Only send to. For the away message you also choose a **schedule**: Always send, Custom schedule, or Outside of business hours.

head: Message
Example text
rows: Welcome to Kemi's Kitchen! Tap Catalog to see today's menu. Order by 10am for lunch. Payment details are only sent from this number.
Thank you for your message. We are open Mon to Sat, 8am to 6pm, and will reply first thing tomorrow.

blocks.text: 3. Quick replies

Open Business tools, **Quick replies**, tap Add, type the message and give it a **shortcut** word. In any chat, type **/** and the shortcut, such as /price or /delivery, and the full message appears to send. Quick replies can include an image or a document too, such as your price list. Create quick replies for the five questions you answer most.

items: /thanks: Thank you for your order! We will confirm delivery time shortly.
/pay: Please pay to (your account name and bank). Send a screenshot after payment. We confirm on our bank app before dispatch.
/delivery: Delivery within Ikeja is about 1,500 naira (approximate). Outside Lagos we use waybill.
/hours: We are open Monday to Saturday, 8am to 6pm.

blocks.text: 4. Labels

Labels are coloured tags you attach to chats or messages. WhatsApp Business starts you with labels such as **New customer, New order, Pending payment, Paid** and **Order complete**, and you can rename them or add your own. Press and hold a chat, tap the label icon and choose. Then filter your chats by label to see, for example, everyone who still owes payment.

blocks.title: An order moving through labels
items: New customer
New order
Pending payment
Paid
Order complete
blocks.caption: Move each chat to the next label as the order progresses, and nothing gets lost.

blocks.title: Worked example: a Friday rush handled calmly
blocks.context: For example, Kemi runs Kemi's Kitchen in Lagos. On Friday morning 23 office workers message her between 8am and 10am.
steps: Each first-time customer automatically receives her greeting with the catalogue tip. Six of them send cart orders straight from the catalogue.
For questions she types /delivery and /pay instead of typing each answer.
She labels each chat New order, then moves it to Pending payment after sending /pay.
At 10:30 she filters by Pending payment, sees 4 chats, and sends a polite reminder to each.
After confirming each payment in her bank app, not from screenshots alone, she labels the chat Paid, and after delivery, Order complete.
blocks.result: All 23 orders are tracked. At the end of the day the Order complete filter shows exactly how many lunches she sold.

blocks.title: Use the WhatsApp Business app on a laptop
blocks.text: If you type a lot of replies, link WhatsApp Business to a laptop with Linked devices. Labels and quick replies make answering even faster with a full keyboard.
Common setup mistakes

items: **Greeting that says too much.** Keep it to three or four short lines with one action, such as Tap Catalog.
**Away message left on Always send.** Customers think you are never available. Use Outside of business hours or a custom schedule.
**Catalogue with dark or blurry photos.** Retake them in daylight; the catalogue is your shop window.
**Quick replies with old prices.** Review them whenever prices change.
**Too many labels.** Five to seven well-used labels are better than twenty unused ones.

blocks.text: Set a reminder to review all four tools once a month: remove sold-out catalogue items, update prices, read your greeting and away messages again, and clear old labels.

takeaways: Catalogue items need clear photos, names, prices or price on request, and descriptions.
Greeting goes to new customers or after 14 days quiet; away messages follow a schedule.
Type / plus a shortcut to send a saved quick reply.
Labels like New order, Pending payment and Paid track every order.

activity.title: Switch on the business engine
steps: Add at least five products or services to your catalogue in one collection.
Write and switch on a greeting message and an away message set to Outside of business hours.
Create four quick replies: thanks, payment, delivery and hours.
Label your last five customer chats with the right stage.
activity.evidence: Screenshots of your catalogue, quick replies list and a chat list filtered by a label.

lessons.title: Customer care habits and spotting WhatsApp scams
objectives: Apply customer service habits that build repeat business
Get customer permission before sending promotional messages
Recognise the common WhatsApp scams aimed at sellers and buyers
Respond safely when you suspect a scam or a hacked account

blocks.text: Tools alone do not make a good WhatsApp business. Customers return to sellers who reply politely, keep promises and treat their information with care. And because money moves through WhatsApp conversations, sellers and buyers are targets for fraud. This lesson covers both: habits that win trust, and the warning signs of scams.

blocks.name: happy-customer
blocks.alt: A smiling customer giving a positive review
blocks.caption: Polite, prompt, honest service is what brings customers back on WhatsApp.

blocks.text: Customer care habits

items: **Reply quickly in business hours.** Even "Received, I will check and reply by 2pm" is better than silence.
**Greet and use names.** "Good morning Mrs Okoro" feels personal.
**Confirm orders in writing** with item, quantity, total, delivery date and address.
**Keep promises on delivery times.** If there is a delay, tell the customer before they ask.
**Ask before adding people** to broadcast lists, groups or channels, and remove anyone who asks.
**Protect customer data.** Do not share customers' numbers, addresses or chats with others or post them on Status without permission.
**Ask for feedback** after delivery, and share reviews only with permission.

blocks.title: Respect opt-in
blocks.text: WhatsApp's business policies expect businesses to message people who have given permission to be contacted. Sending unwanted promotions leads people to block and report you, and many reports can get a business account restricted.
Common WhatsApp scams to recognise

head: Scam
How it looks
What to do
rows: "I sent my code to you by mistake, please send it back"
Never share any code. Turn on two-step verification
A new number with a relative's or boss's photo: "This is my new number, I need urgent money"
Call the person's old number or ask a question only they can answer
A screenshot or SMS showing payment, then pressure to release goods
Confirm in your own bank or Opay or Moniepoint app before releasing goods
"I paid 50,000 naira by mistake instead of 5,000, refund the balance"
Check your real balance; refunds only after the money is truly in your account
Strangers add you to groups promising daily profits for liking videos or trading
Exit, report and block; never pay to earn
"Your account will be blocked, click here" or fake promo and grant links
Do not click; go to the official app or website yourself

blocks.title: Red flags in any message
items: Urgent pressure to act now
Request for code or PIN
Unknown or new number
Payment before checking
Link you did not expect
Too good to be true
blocks.caption: One red flag means slow down; two or more means stop and verify.

blocks.title: Worked example: a fake credit alert at the counter
blocks.context: For example, Rose sells phone accessories in Computer Village, Ikeja. A buyer orders a power bank and earbuds totalling 38,000 naira (approximate) on WhatsApp and arrives at her shop.
steps: The buyer shows a transfer screenshot and says, "I have paid, please hurry, my driver is waiting."
Rose notices the pressure, a red flag, and opens her own Moniepoint app to check incoming transfers.
No payment of 38,000 naira has arrived. She politely says she releases goods only when the money shows in her account.
The buyer leaves. Rose labels the chat, reports and blocks the number, and adds a line to her /pay quick reply: "Goods are released after payment reflects in our account."
blocks.result: Rose avoids losing 38,000 naira of stock, and her quick reply now sets the rule for every customer in advance.

blocks.text: If something goes wrong

items: **Hacked account:** reinstall or open WhatsApp and verify your number again to log the other person out, then turn on two-step verification. Tell contacts through other channels not to send money.
**Report and block** scam numbers from their chat or contact info. Reporting sends recent messages to WhatsApp for review.
**Money lost:** contact your bank or payment app immediately through its official app or customer care, and report to the police.
**Contact WhatsApp:** use Settings, Help, Contact us inside the app.

blocks.title: Three rules that stop most scams
blocks.text: Never share your six-digit code or two-step PIN. Never release goods or refunds until money reflects in your own banking app. Always verify urgent money requests by calling the person on a number you already know.
Handling complaints well

Every business gets complaints: a late delivery, a wrong size, a damaged item. Handled well, a complaint can win a customer for life. Reply quickly and calmly, thank the customer for telling you, and ask for a photo if something arrived damaged. Offer a clear solution, such as a replacement, a repair or a refund, and say when it will happen. Keep the conversation in the private chat, not on Status or in a group. Afterwards, add the Order complete label only when the customer confirms she is satisfied, and note what went wrong so it does not happen again.

takeaways: Reply promptly, confirm orders in writing and keep delivery promises.
Message only people who agreed to hear from you, and protect their data.
Check payments in your own banking app, never by screenshot.
Verify urgent money requests by calling a known number; report and block scammers.

quiz.q: Kemi wants customers who message after 6pm to get an automatic reply saying when she will respond. What should she set up?
options: An away message scheduled Outside of business hours
quiz.explain: Away messages can be scheduled Outside of business hours, which uses the hours in her business profile.

quiz.q: Which shortcut format sends a saved quick reply in WhatsApp Business?
quiz.explain: Typing / and the shortcut word brings up the saved quick reply.

quiz.q: A buyer shows a transfer screenshot and pressures Ada to release goods quickly. What should Ada do?
options: Release the goods, a screenshot is proof
Check her own banking app and release only when the money reflects
quiz.explain: Screenshots and SMS alerts can be faked. Only her own banking app confirms payment.

quiz.q: Nkechi's number is 0816 555 0123. What is her correct WhatsApp short link?
quiz.explain: Use the country code 234 and drop the first zero, with no plus sign or spaces.

quiz.q: Kemi wants to see which customers still owe money. Which tool helps most?
options: Filtering chats by the Pending payment label
quiz.explain: Labels track each order stage, and filtering by Pending payment shows who still needs to pay.

quiz.q: Which business profile description is strongest?
options: Handmade shea butter creams for dry skin, 250g and 500g. Delivery in Abuja. Tap Catalog to order.
quiz.explain: It follows the formula: what, for whom, where or how, and one action.

finalQuiz.q: Which step gives the strongest protection if a fraudster gets your SMS verification code?
options: Having two-step verification with your own six-digit PIN
finalQuiz.explain: With two-step verification on, registering your number on a new phone also needs your PIN, so the SMS code alone is not enough.

finalQuiz.q: Bisi's phone is stolen. What will most help her get her chats back on a new phone?
options: A chat backup to Google Drive or iCloud made before the theft
finalQuiz.explain: Chats are stored on the phone. Only a backup made beforehand can be restored on a new phone.

finalQuiz.q: A message shows one grey tick for a whole day. Which is a possible reason?
options: It was delivered but not opened
The person's phone is off or offline, or they blocked you
finalQuiz.explain: One grey tick means sent but not delivered, often because the phone is offline or the sender is blocked.

finalQuiz.q: Which file type should a tailor use to send a customer a clean, printable price list?
options: A PDF sent as a Document
finalQuiz.explain: Documents arrive uncompressed and can be saved and printed.

finalQuiz.q: Halima wants product photos to look sharp for customers. What should she do before sending?
options: Send it to a broadcast list
finalQuiz.explain: The HD option sends higher quality photos and videos, at the cost of more data.

finalQuiz.q: Who can see Tola's WhatsApp status if her privacy is set to My contacts?
options: Contacts she saved who have also saved her number
finalQuiz.explain: Status is shown to saved contacts who have also saved your number, within your status privacy choice.

finalQuiz.q: A church wants to send weekly announcements to the whole town without exposing anyone's phone number. Which tool fits best?
finalQuiz.explain: Channels are one-way and hide phone numbers of both admins and followers.

finalQuiz.q: What happens when a customer replies to your broadcast list message?
options: Everyone on the list sees the reply
The reply goes to a new group
The reply comes to you privately in your chat with that customer
finalQuiz.explain: Broadcast messages arrive as private chats, so replies come only to you.

finalQuiz.q: In a WhatsApp community, where do admins post a notice that must reach every member?
finalQuiz.explain: Every community has an announcement group that includes all members.

finalQuiz.q: When is a WhatsApp Business greeting message sent automatically?
options: When a customer messages you for the first time or after 14 days with no messages
finalQuiz.explain: The greeting goes to new customers, or to customers who have not chatted with you for 14 days.

finalQuiz.q: Rose types /pay in a customer chat. What happens?
options: WhatsApp sends money to the customer
Her saved quick reply with payment details appears to send
finalQuiz.explain: Typing / followed by the shortcut brings up a saved quick reply.

finalQuiz.q: A new number with your sister's photo says, "This is my new line, send 20,000 naira urgently." What should you do?
options: Send the money, it is urgent
Forward the message to your family group
Call your sister on the number you already know before doing anything
finalQuiz.explain: Impersonation scams rely on urgency. Verifying through a known number exposes the fraud.

capstone.title: My Safe and Professional WhatsApp Setup
capstone.brief: Produce a portfolio showing a secured WhatsApp account and a working WhatsApp Business setup (or, if you do not sell, a community communication setup) that you actually use, with written rules for safety and service.
steps: Secure your account: privacy settings reviewed, two-step verification on, chat backup running, linked devices checked.
Organise your communication: contacts renamed, key chats pinned, busy groups muted, one broadcast list or group with a clear description and rules.

Set up WhatsApp Business: complete profile, at least five catalogue items, greeting and away messages, four quick replies and labels in use. If you do not sell, design a community or group structure for an organisation you belong to instead.
Create your short link and QR code and place them where customers or members will see them.
Write a one-page safety and service sheet: your customer care rules, payment confirmation rule and the three rules that stop most scams.
Run your setup for one week and write a short reflection on what worked and what you will change.

Screenshots of your business profile, catalogue, quick replies and a label filter (or your community or group design)
